paper.name: The Meridian Pilot
paper.masthead_line: THE MERIDIAN PILOT · Meridian's own paper since 1871 · 25p · Tuesday and Friday
rules: A story prints only what Alison Sedman knows and chose to write (D56, ER-PAPER-01): every item has a source_fact and an alison_knows.
The fixed items of an issue come from events the town can know (the Board's notices, the council's notices, the posters, the court list, the club's result).
Items marked state_dependent print only when print_if holds; items marked story_check are re-checked against production/lane/story/frame/ once it is final.
No real event, person, party, club, brand or product; the canon content rule applies to every line; British spelling; pounds and pence plain.
A story about Tom is only as sure as what she was told: see strength_wording.

issues.headline: TWO QUAY BERTHS TO CLOSE FOR WALL REPAIRS

items.story: Berths 3 and 4 on the Hook quay will close to all shipping from Monday 5 November while the quay wall is repaired, the Harbour Board has announced. Masters should apply to the Harbour Master's office for other berths.
items.alison_knows: copied from the typed notice posted on the Harbour Board's door

items.story: The chapel roof fund holds a jumble sale at the chapel hall on Saturday 20 October. Doors open at 2 pm; clothing, books and bric-a-brac, teas and cakes, admission 20p. Father Walsh says the roof will not see another winter.
items.alison_knows: told by Father Walsh, at the chapel hall door

items.story: Police are appealing for witnesses after a shop window on Quay Street was smashed between 11 pm and 1 am on Friday 12 October. Anyone who saw or heard anything is asked to ring the incident room on 960 640.
items.alison_knows: read off the appeal and a word with the constable on the beat

items.story: The Tivoli's new thriller, The Fourth Witness, opens on Thursday. Performances at 5.15 and 8.00, all seats £2.80, pensioners and the unwaged £1.50.
Hookside Rovers drew 1-1 with Easterby United at Ropewalk Park on Saturday, the equaliser coming three minutes from time.
items.alison_knows: her sports desk sheet; she was at the ground

issues.headline: CHAPEL ROOF: SATURDAY'S JUMBLE SALE, AND WHY IT MATTERS

items.story: The lead on the chapel roof is gone from the vestry side, and what is left leaks, Father Walsh told the Pilot. Saturday's sale in the chapel hall is the fund's first this winter.
items.alison_knows: told by Father Walsh; she was shown the damp

items.story: A man who gave his name as a docker was fined £40 by Meridian magistrates on Thursday for driving without due care on the Dock Road.
items.alison_knows: court list; she sat in the press seat

items.story: The Harbour Board is advertising for a quay labourer. Applications in writing, giving age and experience, to the Secretary, to arrive by Friday 16 November. Wages by agreement.
The Copper Row market runs on Tuesdays, Fridays and Saturdays from 8 am to 4 pm. New stalls are welcome; enquiries to the market office.
Tide table: high water at the Hook is 0542 and 1807 on Thursday 1 November, with 4.4 m and 4.3 m, the Harbour Board's table shows.
items.alison_knows: the Board's table, which she copies each month

issues.headline: POLL TAX: MEETING AT THE CHAPEL HALL ON THURSDAY

items.story: Meridian Against the Poll Tax holds a public meeting at the chapel hall on Thursday 25 October at 7.30 pm. Everyone is welcome. The group says it will explain what to do if a summons arrives.
items.alison_knows: a leaflet put through the Pilot's door; she will be there

items.story: Quay Print's machine broke down on Friday and the Hook's bills went out a day late, the printer admits. It says the repair cost £140.
The Tivoli's comedy A Week at Gullwing follows on Thursday 25 October. The Fourth Witness plays until Wednesday.
The ferry's winter service runs half-hourly until 5.30 pm, with the last crossing from the Hook at 11.00 pm Monday to Saturday.
items.alison_knows: the timetable on the ramp board

items.story: Mrs Edith Stockill, of the newsagent's pension counter, has helped fill in forms for 31 neighbours this year and says nobody has yet had a form turned down.
items.alison_knows: Alison asked her at the counter

issues.headline: ADVICE EVENING FOR THOSE WITH A SUMMONS

items.story: Meridian Against the Poll Tax will hold an advice evening at the chapel hall on Tuesday 30 October at 7 pm for anyone who has had a summons. The advice is free and confidential.
items.alison_knows: the group's sheet, and she went on Thursday

items.story: A van was stolen from the quay in the early hours of Saturday 20 October. Police say anyone with information should ring 960 640.
items.alison_knows: police appeal; one of the quay men told her he heard it start

items.story: Hookside Rovers lost 0-2 at Thornwick Town. The manager says the pitch did not suit them.
Mr Walter Pybus, who delivered the Pilot on the Hook for thirty years, has retired. The paper wishes him a long rest.
items.alison_knows: a note from the circulation desk

items.story: The planning notice for 7 Quay Street, which would turn the empty shop into an estate agent's office, has been up since Monday. Comments to the Planning Officer by Friday 9 November.
items.alison_knows: read off the notice in its sleeve

issues.headline: WHAT THE CHAPEL HALL HEARD ON THURSDAY

items.story: About ninety people crowded the chapel hall on Thursday night for the meeting against the poll tax. The meeting agreed to march on Saturday 10 November, assembling at the Exchange at 11 am.
A man was assaulted near the quay on the night of Sunday 28 October, between 10 pm and 11 pm. The police ask anyone who saw anything to ring the incident room, 960 640.
items.alison_knows: police appeal; she asked at the station
items.print_if: a man was assaulted near the quay on the night of Sunday 28 October (a deed in the town)

items.story: Quay Street will be closed to traffic on Sunday 4 November from 8 am to 6 pm for gas main renewal. Pedestrians may pass. The diversion is by Weighhouse Lane.
Hookside Rovers beat Fenby Albion 2-0 at Ropewalk Park.
The caff on the quay will open its back room for the Harbour Board's staff on Friday dinner times, Mrs Grace Rinaldi says. Tea stays at 30p.

items.story: Professional wrestling comes to the Drill Hall tonight at 7.30. Ringside £4, unreserved £2.50, tickets at the door.
Quay Street will be dug up on Sunday for the gas main. Householders are asked to move cars off the street by Saturday night.
The Harbour Board has confirmed that the wall repairs to berths 3 and 4 begin on Monday. Two coasters have been moved to the far quay.

items.story: Customs officers at the dock gate seized 3,000 cigarettes from a van on Wednesday. The driver was released pending inquiries.
items.alison_knows: told by a customs officer at the gate; Alison saw the van go in

items.story: Meridian Against the Poll Tax says 200 people have signed up for the march on 10 November.

items.story: The planning application for the empty shop at 7 Quay Street has drawn three letters of objection, the Planning Officer says. Comments close on Friday.

items.story: Holt's garage on Cold Store Road has taken delivery of a new recovery truck and says it will pull anything off the quay road, day or night.
Hookside Rovers lost 1-3 at Saltmarsh Athletic. The next home game is on Saturday.

items.story: Meridian Against the Poll Tax will march tomorrow, Saturday 10 November, assembling at the Exchange at 11 am. Marchers are asked to bring neighbours and banners.

items.story: The Hook's chip shop on Back Parade is to open on Sundays from this week, Mr Dobson says, to catch the ferry trade.

items.story: Comments on the planning application for 7 Quay Street close today.

issues.headline: THOUSANDS MARCH FROM THE EXCHANGE

items.story: Marchers assembled at the Exchange on Saturday against the poll tax and walked to the town hall. The police counted 800; the organisers said 1,500. There was no trouble.
A boxing night is to be held at the Drill Hall on Friday 16 November. Ten bouts, first bout 7.30 pm, ringside £3, unreserved £1.50.
items.alison_knows: the boxing club's secretary rang her

items.story: The old-time and sequence dance is back at the chapel hall on Saturday 17 November, 7.30 to 11 pm, with live music, tea and sandwiches. Admission £1.50, all welcome.
Hookside Rovers beat Northwold Rangers 3-1 at Ropewalk Park, their first home win since September.
The council's licensing committee meets on Thursday 15 November. Its agenda includes the renewal of private hire operators' licences.

items.story: Meridian Ferry's winter timetable is unchanged. The last crossing leaves the Hook at 11.00 pm.
Hookside Rovers lost 0-1 at Fenby Albion. The manager says the better team lost.
The grocer on Quay Street is offering eggs at 85p a dozen and tinned pears two for 69p this week.

items.story: Mrs Winifred Duggleby, who cleans the chapel, has given the chapel hall a new set of cups.

items.story: The Harbour Board has taken on two men as quay labourers from the applications made by 16 November. The Board says the wall repairs are on time.
The dock gate will be chained to vehicles from the early morning of Saturday 1 December, the Board says, pending a review of who may pass.

The Tivoli's next programme begins on Thursday 29 November.

Hookside Rovers beat Easterby United 2-0 on Saturday to go fourth.
Police have recovered a stolen van from a lock-up on North Road. No arrests have been made.

letters.from: Mickey Suddaby (a copy of the letter he left)
letters.title: The letter that came with the will
body: If you are reading this I have not had the manners to say it to your face. The office is yours, and the flat above it. Sheila knows the book. Ron knows the door.
Do not let anybody tell you what is owed before you have read the book. Do not let anybody tell you what you are, either.

1 Quay Street
Meridian

letters.title: Premises: 1 Quay Street
body: We act for the owners of the freehold of the parade on Quay Street, of which your premises form part. We understand that you have lately succeeded to the occupation of the office and the flat above it.

Rent is collected each Friday by our clients' agent, who will call at the counter. We should be glad if you would call at our offices at your earliest convenience, so that the terms of your occupation may be confirmed in writing.

letters.title: Your private hire licence
body: We write on behalf of a client who has raised with the Council certain concerns as to the condition of the vehicles operated from your premises, and as to the keeping of records under the conditions of your operator's licence.
The Council's Licensing Section will write to you separately to arrange an inspection of the cars. We should be glad to see you at our offices should you wish to discuss the matter before then.

Please have each car's log, test certificate and insurance available. Any defect found will be noted and you will have seven days to put it right.

body: I write to inform you that an officer of this Department will call at your premises on Monday 26 November 1990 at 9 am to inspect your records for value added tax, under the Value Added Tax Act 1983.

He will wish to see your books of account, including the record of fares, the records of the vehicles, the payroll and the purchase invoices, for the period since you took over the business. You may produce each item on the morning it is asked for, or ask for it to be put in writing and produced the next day. You may ask for this twice.
I should be grateful if you would arrange for the books to be available. The inspection will last a week and the books will be closed at five o'clock on the last afternoon.

open_points: Paper name: The Meridian Pilot, minted here (chosen). The prototype's 'Evening Mail' is a real title and is retired; so is its cigarette 'Mariners' as a paper-shop line (kept as a fictional brand 'Mariner').

Six owed brands minted (chosen, for his tap): Hookside Rovers (club), The Meridian Pilot (paper), Cutter FM (pirate radio), Estuary Television (TV), Tidewire Telephones (operator, the kiosk's mark), Realm Post (postal cypher). The brand bible file (content/brands/brand-bible-v1.json) is not in the repository; the entries follow its field list.

Numbers and names in the frozen map override the cloud week's fascias: the older target numbered the newsagent 18, ironmonger 16, tea rooms 14 and used 'FISH MARKET', 'STEAM LAUNDRY' and 'FAMILY GROCER' as names; the map has Laverack's (3), the Washeteria (9), Hook Stores (11), Peart's (8), the ironmonger's (10), the Copper Kettle (12). The fascias here follow the map. The cloud week's pictures were built to the old names and will not match; the keeper should decide whether the pictures are rebuilt.

The held names of the cloud week (the Sanderling Trio, the wrestlers' ring names, the Drill Hall, The Fourth Witness, A Week at Gullwing, Marshland Pictures, Meridian Against the Poll Tax, Quay Print) are adopted as chosen. The estate agent on the letting boards is Agar & Co, not the held Armitage & Stobbs, because the frozen map's estate agent is Agar's agents at 2 Cold Store Road.
The telephone numbers use a six-digit local form (960 xxx). Mickey's is 960 418; the older target's '0632 960418' is not used (0632 is a real code).
The Drill Hall, the Exchange, the town hall, the Tivoli and Copper Row are not on the frozen map (off the Hook); posters name them as venues only.

Rent is £18 (blueprint 2.7.4 and economy), not the story bibles' £38. The rent man is minted as Mr Leonard Askew of Agar & Co's agents (chosen); the story frame lists Dawn Pybus as running for the rent collector.

story_check: every letter or note that rests on a story beat (Mickey's letter, Agar's first and licence letters, the council's inspection and hearing, the Customs letter and its five mornings, the cold-store contract, the notes of June, Cammack and Ellis) is marked story_check and its date or day is chosen; the frame in production/lane/story/frame/ is a draft. The Customs officer's name Hebblewhite and Agar's clerk Ombler are the frame's proposals.
Customs and Excise, the Value Added Tax Act 1983 and 999 are real public bodies, an Act and a number; the blueprint itself names Customs and Excise. No crest, logo or real person is shown.

Items in the paper that report a fixed date but depend on a state (the 28 October assault, the licensing hearing, the Customs visits, the dock gate chain) carry print_if and print only when the state holds; the dock gate chaining on Saturday 1 December is the frame's proposal.

Prices in print: tea 30p, breakfast £1.80, dinner £2.50, fares 80p plus £1.10 a mile, the paper 25p, 20 cigarettes £1.70, fish and chips £1.60, milk 30p, loaf 52p, key cut £1.50, crowbar £6, torch £4, barber £4, rooms £25 a week, second-hand coats £15, jackets £45, overcoats £90 (economy files). Fish prices of the older target changed to cod £2.60 and haddock £2.40; the other prices are the older target's or chosen, marked.
The Tom story templates need Alison to hold the fact; their wording follows strength_wording. 'Kill' is only ever printed as a police statement about a body, never as a rumour.
